resources.string: Voice Messages
What Voice asks a session for you shows as a Voice message, marked with a waveform.
Attach With +
The + menu grows out of the message box with Camera, Photos, and Files. Hold + and slide to choose in one motion.
Photos opens right above the message box; tap photos to attach them.
The camera has lens buttons, pinch to zoom, tap to focus, and flash.
Hold +, slide up to Photos, and let go
Steadier Calls
A patchy connection costs a call a brief glitch instead of seconds of silence.
Mute Sessions
Muted sessions stay in your list but never join Catch Up or show an unread dot.
Hold Catch Up to mark everything as read. Sessions waiting on you stay.
Hold a session in the drawer and tap Mute
Pair From Anywhere
Run opencode pair --remote on your computer to connect from any network, without shared Wi-Fi or Tailscale.
Scan the code it shows, or paste the link it prints.
Run opencode pair --remote, then add the server on your phone
When Sessions Were Active
Drag the session list toward the session to see when each was last active.
Swiping left over the list closes it.
Open the session list and drag it to the right
Dictate and Send
Tap the mic to dictate, then send straight from the recording bar, or tap Stop to review it first.
Hold the mic to talk, slide up to lock, or slide left to cancel.
Recording keeps going when you leave the app, with a Live Activity to stop it.
Switch sessions mid-recording and Send goes to the one on screen.
Tap the mic, say a sentence, and tap Send
App Actions and Shortcuts
Start a call or a session, or send a message, from Google Assistant’s App Actions, app shortcuts, or Quick Settings.
Hold the app icon for your recent sessions.
Say “Hey Google, start a voice call in OpenCode”
Status Orb
An orb beside Working and on subagent cards shows what the agent is doing, and turns into the copy button when it finishes.
Shell Activity
A running shell’s >_ prompt laps as its output arrives.
Math and Diagrams
Replies typeset math and draw Mermaid diagrams.
Tap a diagram to zoom in, or hold it to see its source.
Math follows your text size.
Ask for a flowchart of how a message is sent
Draw a flowchart of how a message is sent
Notify When Done
Get a notification when a session you started here finishes, with a short summary of what happened.
Turn on Always Notify in a session’s sheet to hear about every reply, even ones started on your computer.
Tap a notification to open its session.
Send a message, then lock your phone
Switch Servers
The server you’re on is the drawer’s title. Tap it to switch to another server or add one.
Settings shows the connection as a live heartbeat, with the round trip beside the server’s name.
Rename a server; only this phone uses the name.
Open the drawer, tap the server’s name, and add your other computer
Images Like Photos
Images show whole in the session and open like Photos: pinch to zoom, swipe between them, and drag down to close.
Every file the agent names opens in the app.
Share saves anything you open to Photos or Files, videos and audio included.
Ask the agent to read a few screenshots, then tap one and drag it down
Voice Calls
Tap the waveform in an empty message box and talk. Voice works in your sessions while you talk and tells you when the work is done.
Ask for any session by name: Voice opens it and starts or steers work there.
Talk over it to interrupt, or ask how the work is going.
Tap the call bar for live captions.
Mute and End from the call’s notification, on the Lock Screen too.
Touch and hold Stop to call while the agent works.
Choose a voice in Settings → Voice.
Start a call and say “open my upload fixes session and check the tests”
Tidier Drawer
Rows start on one edge, status dots sit at the end of each row, and search is a button at the top.
Long Pastes as Cards
A long paste becomes a Pasted Text card beside your images, and the agent still reads all of it.
Tap the card to read the whole paste, with Copy and Share.
Long messages fold to a few lines with Show More.
Copy a long log, paste it into the message box, and tap the card
Works on Weak Signal
A few seconds without signal no longer fails anything. Sends, sessions, and calls wait for the connection and carry on.
Send is always ready, and messages go in the order you sent them.
A message that couldn’t send stays in place with Retry, and retrying never sends it twice.
When your server is offline, its name in the drawer dims. Tap it for Try Again.
Open a session as your train goes into a tunnel
Start in Any Project
New Session lists your recent projects above the message box, and All Projects can open any folder on your computer.
The project you chose stays above the message box as you type.
A call started from a new session works in the project you chose.
Tap New Session, then All Projects, then Choose Folder…
Steer While It Works
Send while the agent works and it reads your message at its next step, moving long commands to the background first.
Touch and hold Send to choose Steer or Queue for one message.
Hold a waiting message to move it to the queue or delete it.
Stop reads Stopping… at once, and a steering message you sent runs next.
While a long command runs, send a message and watch the command move to the background
In-App Browser Pages
With the In-App Browser experiment on, a link pushes its page in over the session. Swipe from the edge to go back.
Answer From the Message Box
Questions and permissions grow out of the message box, and you answer right there: tap a choice, or type or dictate your own.
Permissions show the command or edit before you allow it.
Deny takes what you typed as what to do instead, so the agent keeps going.
Your draft comes back once you’ve answered.
When the agent asks a question, hold the mic and say your answer
Pick Up Where You Left Off

Coming back to a session opens it at the bottom, with what arrived while you were away already there. To open a long backlog at a New line instead, turn on New Messages Divider in Settings › Sessions.
Sessions you’re likely to open refresh as the drawer opens, so they’re ready when you tap.
Switching back keeps a session’s background work and context gauge while it refreshes.
Start a long task, switch to another session, and come back once it has replied
New Model Picker
Choose a model and its thinking level from the Model sheet, with your favorites on top. To try the list that grows out of the message box, turn on New Model Picker in Settings → Experimental.
Use the Thinking menu in the Model sheet when a model offers levels.
Swipe a model to add it to Favorites.
A quiet line in the session marks where you switched model or level.
Tap the model in the message box and choose a thinking level
When a Run Fails
A run that stops early says why in plain words, with one way forward: Edit, Compact, Switch Model, or Try Again.
Edit undoes your message and puts it back in the message box to reword.
Hold the line to see the full error and copy it.
When the agent will retry on its own, Working counts down to the next try.
When a reply is blocked, tap Edit, reword the message, and send it again
Keyboard Closes Cleanly
Dragging the keyboard away no longer leaves a gap under the last message.
Send From the Share Sheet
Share anything to OpenCode, pick a session, add a message, and send it without opening the app.
Your recent sessions appear in the share sheet’s top row.
JSON files and exports attach as files with their names intact.
Continue in OpenCode opens the session with what you shared in the message box.
If it can’t send, Send Later sends it the next time you open the app.
Share a screenshot to OpenCode, type a question, and tap Send
Badge on the App Icon
The app icon shows how many sessions are unread or waiting on you, the same count as Catch Up.
Muted sessions don’t count.
It needs notifications turned on.
Leave a session waiting on a question, then go to the Home Screen
Keyboard Slides With the Drawer
Opening the session list while typing keeps your message focused, and the keys slide aside with the session.
What’s New, Simpler
What’s New opens as a page like Settings, with a page for each feature and fixes gathered here.
Catch Up Returns to the Drawer
Leaving Catch Up takes you back to the session list as you left it.
Days in the Transcript
A session that runs across days shows the day over the first message of each one, like “Wednesday 8:24 AM”, and the time over a message sent after an hour’s pause.
Days read Today, Yesterday, or the weekday within the week, otherwise the date.
Steering and queued messages get no stamp while they wait.
Open a session you started earlier in the week and scroll up
Link Previews
Links under a reply show what they are, one line each: a pull request or issue with its title and state, a commit, a video, a page.
GitHub pull requests, issues, commits and repositories show their title, with Open, Merged or Closed in colour.
X posts show who posted and what they said; YouTube links show their title, and other pages a name read from the link.
Three links show; tap “more” beside Copy for the rest, and again to fold them away.
Hold a link for a bigger preview, Copy Link, and Share.
Ask the agent what changed in a repository this week
What changed in a GitHub repository I use this week? Include links.
Rolling Numbers
Live counts in the background-work capsule, the Session sheet, Used N rows, and Catch Up roll digit by digit.
Grouped Messages
Messages you send in a row sit together as one block, and steering messages waiting for the agent share one Steering label.
Bubbles in a row sit close, their corners joining where they meet.
Photos and files keep their own round shape inside the block.
As the agent takes each message, it moves up into place in one motion.
While the agent works, send three quick messages, one with a photo
Quiet Tool and Question Rows
Tool groups and answered questions open onto a full-width band like code, with consecutive reads merged into one row.
Collapsed groups read “Used N tools” and mark failed tool calls in red.
Execute rows name the tools their script called, and Skill rows name the skill.
Answered questions show the prompt and every option offered, with your choice checked.
Tap a “Used N tools” row in a session to open its band
Playground Controls on Mac
With Developer Mode on, pair tuning with your Mac to replay playground animations in slow motion and inspect captured frames.
The Mac’s knobs page holds playground selection, presets and replay controls; the phone shows only the playground.
Compact cards show which controls are on screen, with named presets for motion and spacing and Native to restore the shipped feel; each preset applies its values together in one update.
The floating tuning panel hides when the Mac connects; summon it with the tuning gesture and choose Exit Playground to leave.
Seeded scenarios replay the same sample session so you can compare motion between builds.
Replays start fresh and deliver their steering and queued messages instead of leaving them waiting.
The Mac’s Review Player lets you step through captured geometry, mark a frame, and send animation feedback.
Open Settings → Developer, pair with the Mac tuning page, then try Transcript → Stream Reply at 0.25×
Easier Swipes in Catch Up
A quick flick or shorter drag in Catch Up sends the card on its way instead of snapping it back.
Clearer Settings
Find experimental features and developer tools in Settings → Experimental, in-app notices in Notifications, and call history in Voice.
Reliable Sends
Messages retry automatically if iOS briefly rejects an already-working server connection.
Steadier Keyboard and Menus
Tap + while typing to open attachments without lowering the keyboard or moving the controls; the header blur stays in place as the keyboard moves.
Links Open in Their Apps
A link opens in the app that handles it, like GitHub or YouTube; with the In-App Browser experiment on, hold a link and choose Open in App Browser.
Easier-to-Scan Session List
Pinned and Recents step back in smaller grey type, unread and waiting sessions stand out in medium weight, and read ones dim slightly.
Tidier Queued Messages
The queued messages sheet is only as tall as your queue, with numbered rows and quiet buttons to send a message now or cancel it.
Tiles for a Session
Add a Quick Settings tile to open a session, or start a call in it, with one tap.
The new Open Session tile opens the session you choose.
Start Call can call into a session you choose, or a new session. Unless you change it, it calls the session you viewed last.
Choose from your pinned and recent sessions; the tile shows the session’s current title.
Tiles only open the app: nothing is sent until you speak or type.
Open Quick Settings, tap Edit, and drag OpenCode’s Open Session tile into place
No Keyboard Over Settings
Opening Settings from the drawer while you were typing puts the keyboard away instead of leaving it over Settings.
Roomier Session List
The session list has a larger title and bigger grey Pinned and Recents headers with more room above them; open the drawer to see it.
Fewer “Checking”s on Calls
On a call, the voice reacts to what you said instead of answering every request with “Checking”, and a request you keep talking over is no longer sent twice.
Smoother Streaming Replies

A streaming reply’s newest line fades in without dimming or flicking on, rows no longer stretch past their text and spring back, and list items and headings appear as themselves instead of starting as a stray dash or hash.
Model List as a Sheet
With the New Model Picker experiment on, the message box turns into a sheet of models where the keyboard was, the keyboard goes down, and it folds back smoothly however fast you open and close it.
Whole Queued Count
The queued pill above the composer reads “2 queued” in full instead of cutting it to “2 queu…”, and rolling counts elsewhere keep every character too.
Photos in Place of the Keyboard
With the New Plus Menu experiment on, Photos grows the + menu into a sheet of your photos where the keyboard was, and holding + shows your newest photos: slide to one and let go to add it.
Easier Composer Taps
Buttons in the composer are easier to tap at large text sizes.
A Tick for a New Project
Choosing a different project for a new session, above the message box or in All Projects, gives a light tick.
Fork Opens the Copy
Fork in a session’s details opens the copy again.
Easier Taps
The Session sheet’s title is easier to tap, and VoiceOver and Voice Control no longer reach composer buttons hidden while you dictate.
Image Previews
Images the agent names appear as previews in a bento layout, and missing files say so.
Previews sit under the paragraph that names them.
Tap an image to open it full screen and swipe through the reply’s images.
Images outside the session’s folder wait for you to tap before loading.
Ask the agent to show screenshots from your project.
Show me the screenshots in this project.
Connection Errors Say What Failed
Connection errors show the error code, address tried, and DNS result, with help when a tailnet name resolves outside Tailscale.
Faster Reconnects
Sessions catch up sooner when the server comes back after an outage.
Every Running Subagent
The subagent count above the composer includes ones nested under other subagents and ones in sessions with more than 100, matching the TUI.
Clearer Reply Typography
Level-3 headings step up above bold text, prose softens slightly so bold stands out, and paragraphs and code blocks get a touch more breathing room.
Stay at the Bottom
Sessions stay at the bottom while delayed content loads.
Drafts Stay Put
Drafts, attached photos and locations, and messages waiting to send stay in place if the app closes in the background.
Themes
Give sessions a theme, like Tokyo Night, Catppuccin, Dracula, Rosé Pine or GitHub, with a live preview as you browse.
Themes colour the transcript, your messages, code, syntax, diffs and links.
Mode in Appearance sets light, dark or system.
Controls keep their native Liquid Glass look in every theme.
Open Settings → Appearance → Theme and try Tokyo Night.
Return Key Setting
Turn off Return Key Sends in Settings when you want Return to add a new line, or use Command-Return and Shift-Return on a hardware keyboard.
Quote Replies
Select text in an assistant reply and tap Quote to add it to your message as a quote card.
Launch Bloom
Opening the app from a cold start inhales the OpenCode mark and blooms into your session.
Drag a Session to Pin It
Hold and drag any session up into Pinned to pin it in that spot, or drag a pinned session down into Recents to unpin it.
Smoother Call Button
With the Call Tray experiment on, the call button blends straight into the red End button as a call starts, and back as you hang up, instead of flashing through the background.
Evenly Inset Controls

The composer’s + and mic, the background-work and queued pills’ glyphs, and New Session’s symbol in the sidebar now sit optically centred in the round ends of their glass. The shell glyph is now a circle like the subagent orb, without its blinking cursor, and both show side by side when both are running.
Smoother Dictation with Music
Dictating while music plays keeps it in stereo on AirPods without a dropout a minute later, and on your phone alone it stays on the speaker instead of the earpiece.
A Hand for Interrupted
An interrupted run and an interrupted shell now show a raised hand, and a shell you stop reads Interrupted instead of Stopped.
Snappier Autocomplete
With the Composer Autocomplete experiment on, suggestions keep up as you type, and dragging the list scrolls it without picking a row.
Grouped Experiments
Experiments in Settings → Experimental are grouped, and calls have one Call Style choice.
Model Picker as a Standard Sheet

With the New Model Picker experiment on, the model in the message box opens a standard sheet where each model has its own thinking-level menu. The earlier picker is now Custom Model Picker in Settings › Experimental.
Reports Reach the Session
Report a Problem now also sends your note into the session you reported from, with the full report attached for the agent to read.
The message opens with a problem report line, your note, the report ID and a link to the uploaded trace.
The device, build, screen, timeline and app log arrive as an attached file, like one you attach yourself.
From Home it goes to your most recent session.
If the upload fails, the note and summary still arrive and say so; Try Again then sends just the trace link.
A “Sent to session” confirmation shows when it lands.
Open a session’s menu, choose Report a Problem, add a note and tap Send
Team Scrawl Feedback
Join Team Feedback with your personal link to send three-finger Scrawl recordings and redacted diagnostics to the shared queue on the Problems board.
Open your opencode://team/join link to review what gets collected and accept.
A three-step interactive tutorial walks through holding three fingers, talking and drawing, and sending a practice clip to the test lane.
Each recording attaches the same redacted timeline, app log, and Motion Watch diagnostics as Report a Problem.
Replay the tutorial or leave Team Feedback anytime in Settings › Developer.
Open Settings › Developer to check your Team Feedback status or replay the tutorial.
Faster Scrawl Start
Scrawl’s controls appear while the microphone and recorder start.
Draw, Send and Discard taps are kept while recording gets ready.
A three-finger hold prepares the overlay without starting the microphone early.
Fixed a crash when Scrawl’s microphone restarts during an audio route change.
On a paired device, hold three fingers to start a recording
Call Tray in the Drawer
With the Call Tray experiment on, opening the drawer during a call carries the tray beneath New Session, with its level, Mute and End, and closing brings it back.
Smoother Streaming Replies
Long replies stay quick as they stream, and half-written bold, code and links show formatted instead of as raw Markdown.
Return Adds a New Line
Return now adds a new line by default. Turn on Return Key Sends in Settings › Sessions to send with Return, or use Ctrl+Enter on a hardware keyboard.
Aligned Drawer Controls
Search, New Session and Settings line up with the session’s header and message box on phones and tablets.
Steadier Call Controls
The call waveform keeps moving when you switch sessions, and the controls stay level as you open the session list.
Voice Messages Appear Promptly
Messages Voice sends into the session appear as soon as the server accepts them, even when session updates are delayed.
Image Link Previews
Turn on Image Link Previews in Settings › Experimental › Transcript to preview linked images in replies. Tap a thumbnail to open it full screen and zoom.
Smoother Link Previews
Link previews fade in as they load, and the rows below move smoothly when a title changes height.
Rounded Activity Capsule
The subagent and shell capsule keeps its rounded ends while you press it.
Simpler Advanced Settings
Experiments in Settings › Experimental are all in open groups, the model pickers are one Model Picker choice, and you can tap anywhere on a choice’s row to change it.
Revert to Here
Hold one of your messages and choose Revert to Here to go back to that point and edit it.
The message’s words, photos and files return to the message box.
Undo brings the turns and their file changes back until you send a new message.
It’s offered while the agent isn’t working.
Hold a message you sent earlier and choose Revert to Here.
Drag from the Session
Hold and drag code, images, files, links and messages out of a session into other apps.
Code blocks arrive as text with their language.
Images and files the agent wrote arrive as files.
Drop any of them into the message box to attach or paste them.
Scrolling, selecting text and menus work as before.
Select a line of code in a reply, then hold the selection and drag the block into Notes.
Write a short Swift function that reverses a string, in a code block.
Easier Tuning Controls
The folded tuning pill and edge tab have larger tap targets.
Their glass faces keep the same size.
Fold the Tuning Panel, then tap near the edge of its pill or tab
Steadier Project Picking
Recent folders keep their places as you choose a project, the header name changes softly, and the Project sheet has clearer folder paths.
Quieter Session Loading
A small, still logo fades in only when a session takes a moment to load, then fades into its messages.
Voice Connection Fixes
Grok keeps using your xAI key when your server runs calls, and Gemini identifies itself correctly.
Call Tray Motion
The Call Tray’s waveform follows its rounded edge as it opens and moves into or out of the drawer.
Call Tray Return
The Call Tray stays visible as the drawer closes and the keyboard returns.
Fuller Session Titles
Long session titles in the sidebar run to the edge and fade out instead of stopping early with an ellipsis.
Quicker Call Sounds
A call’s connecting pings start with the first sweep instead of a couple of seconds after you tap.
Calmer Loading
Cached sessions open straight away; a session that takes a moment to load shows pulsing message bubbles that fade into your messages.
Dictation Shows Its End
On iOS 26, a long dictation stopped into a pending request’s reply box shows its last lines instead of text from partway through.
Clearer First Pairing
Pasting with nothing on the clipboard says so beside Paste, and setup no longer promises remote access in half a minute.
Pair from the OpenCode App
The welcome screen points you to Settings → Pairing in OpenCode on your computer, or /pair in the terminal, with the install command for anyone who doesn’t have OpenCode yet.
Session Links
A session ID in a reply shows as that session’s title. Tap it to open the session.
A subagent’s ID opens over the session you’re in, and Back returns.
Hold one to copy its ID.
An ID this server doesn’t know shows shortened.
Ask the agent to name another session by its ID, then tap the title.
List my five most recent OpenCode sessions with their session IDs.
Multiple Windows on Tablets
On a tablet, open sessions in windows of their own and keep two side by side.
Hold a session in the sidebar and choose Open in New Window.
Each window has its own session, sidebar and message box.
Pins, read sessions and your servers are the same in every window.
Windows come back on the session they showed.
Hold a session in the sidebar, choose Open in New Window, and put it beside the first.
Plain Launch
OpenCode opens on a plain screen and switches straight to your session as soon as it’s ready, with no loading animation.
Softer Call Sounds
Calls connect, ping and hang up with soft, breathy tones that sit quietly under the conversation.
Smoother Session List
The sidebar’s session list scrolls smoothly while sessions work, and holding a session opens its menu with the row staying its size.
Open and Try From What’s New
An entry’s page in What’s New has a button that opens its setting, like Themes, or starts a new session with a prompt typed in for you to try.
Project Icon Fixes
With Project Icons enabled, the sidebar also shows icons your server finds in Icon Composer bundles.
New Only When Needed
With the New Messages Divider experiment on, New marks what arrived only when there’s more than fits on screen.
All Caught Up
Reading the last session in Catch Up takes you straight back to the sidebar, where Catch Up checks itself off as All Caught Up.
Mention Sessions
With the Composer Autocomplete experiment on, type @ to mention another session by its title, as on desktop.
GPT-Live Keys
GPT-Live calls can use your own OpenAI key, your server’s OpenAI key, or its OpenCode Console connection.
Pick Up Where You Left Off
After you pair a new computer, the sidebar opens on its recent sessions so you can choose one, instead of leaving you on an empty session.
Choose a Voice Server
In Settings › Voice › Voice Provider, choose which saved server your calls go through, or your own OpenAI account on this phone.
Living Orb Floats Everywhere

Living Orb is now the floating Call Style in Settings › Experimental › Calls. It’s bigger, stays above Settings and every screen, and moves with both voices, each in its own colour when you talk at once. Tap it to grow it into a card, drag up for the whole call and its transcript, and drag down to shrink it back. Orb, beneath Call Style, changes its look.
New Messages Divider
When a reply that arrived while you were away is longer than the screen, the session opens on a New divider at its start.
A reply that fits on screen opens at the end, with no divider.
Replies that stream in while you watch are never marked.
Reading down to the end clears the divider.
Turn it off in Settings › Sessions.
Ask for a long reply, switch to another app until it finishes, then come back.
Composer Follows the Keyboard
The composer’s controls open with the keyboard and move with it as you drag it up and down.
Full-Screen Composer Photos
Tap a photo in the composer to see it full screen, swipe between photos, and remove one before you send.
New Photo Picker
Turn on New Plus Menu in Settings › Experimental › Composer to pick up to 8 recent photos right from the + menu, browse All Photos, and watch them fly into the composer and then into the session.
Lit Project Icons
With Project Icons enabled, sidebar icons catch the light: a soft highlight from the top, a fine glass edge and a gentle shadow.
Session Live Updates
Turn on Session Live Updates in Settings › Experimental › Drawer to follow a run you send in a live notification, on the Lock Screen too, until it’s done or needs your input.
Fix a Refused Sign-In
When a server refuses your password, the sidebar’s server menu offers Edit Server… instead of a Try Again that couldn’t help. The welcome screen now points to opencode pair --remote in the terminal.
Voice Screenshots
On a voice call, say “look at this” and the app’s screen goes to a session with your feedback.
It sends only the app’s own screen, with its screen name and call and app state.
Ask for the call log or recent app logs to go with it; addresses and credentials are masked.
It won’t capture while a sign-in screen or password field is showing.
In a voice call, say “take a screenshot, this row is misaligned”
Background Results in Calls
When a session you asked during a call starts work in the background, the call tells you what it found as soon as it’s done, even after you’ve moved on to other things.
Sound Effects
An experiment that plays soft sounds with the haptics for replies, requests, Catch Up and failed sends.
Silent and vibrate modes mute them, and music keeps playing.
They stay quiet during a call, dictation or media, and in the background.
Volume and an optional Send Sound sit beneath the switch.
Turn on Sound Effects in Settings › Experimental, then wait for a reply in another session
Titles from First Prompts
Sessions without a title now show their first prompt, on one line, until the server names them.
Sessions Settings
Settings has a new Sessions page, where New Messages Divider sits above Return Key Sends, and Advanced is now two rows: Experimental and Developer.
Project Icons On
Project icons now show beside session titles. Turn them off in Settings › Experimental.
Photos Over the Keyboard
With New Plus Menu on, the + menu opens over the keyboard, and Photos grows from it into a sheet that runs to the screen’s edges, then folds back without putting the keyboard away.
Orb Connect Motion
With Living Orb on, the call button lifts into the orb and spins up while the call connects, then lands back in the button when it ends. Redialing right away starts a fresh call instead of sticking.
Orb Presets and Fancy
Orb, beneath Call Style in Settings › Experimental › Calls, now opens on Fancy, with a bigger live preview and a row of presets. Save your own, rename them, and copy or paste a setup to share it.
Smoother Send After a Pause
A message you send after a pause now rises straight from the composer into its bubble, instead of first dipping toward the composer under its time stamp.
Steadier Round Trip
The connection card’s ms number is now a rolling average of the last few checks, so one slow answer nudges it instead of making it jump.
Sidebar Drags Follow Your Finger
A session you drag in the sidebar now stays right under your finger, rides above the header, scrolls the list at its edges, and springs into place when you let go.
Inbox Sidebar

Turn on Inbox Sidebar in Settings › Experimental › Drawer to see your sessions as an inbox: what needs your input first, then unread, each with its project and latest reply. Swipe to mark one read or archive it.
A Ready First Session

Pairing your first computer now opens a new session in its most recent project, with a few questions to try, and a tap confirms you’re connected. A new install also starts with What’s New already read.
Welcome Preview

A new first-run welcome shows OpenCode working on a laptop while a phone steers it, then pairs in one step. Turn on Welcome Preview in Settings › Experimental › Drawer and tap Show Welcome to see it; closing it brings you back.
Select Text in the Composer
Dragging a selection’s handles or the loupe in a draft no longer puts the keyboard away or pulls the composer up or down.
Calls Wait for You to Finish
The voice agent no longer talks over you: updates wait until you’ve finished speaking, and talking over it stops it.
Voice Calls Use Wisp’s Sounds

Calls start with a soft breath over a quiet connecting shimmer, chime when they connect, tick gently as the agent looks, opens or runs things, and sigh when they end. Pick another set in Settings › Voice › Call Sounds.
The Voice Orb Is Now Wisp

The call’s orb now has Wisp’s look: a glass lens over glowing dots that both voices light, with Wisp’s moods for connecting, listening, working, speaking and waiting on you. It’s the only orb style, so the old styles and Orb settings are gone.
Encrypted Notification Previews
With the updated notification plugin and an HTTPS connection, your server encrypts the title and message for this device. If a preview can’t be opened, the notification just says “New activity.”
Sessions Outlive Their Folder
When a session’s folder is gone, like a removed worktree, a failed send offers to move it to its project’s folder and sends again.
Set Up Notifications with OpenCode
In Settings → Notifications, tap Set Up with OpenCode to review a prompt that installs the missing notification plugin.
The Call’s Card Takes Over the Bottom
In Living Orb, the call’s card now fills the bottom of the screen over the message field, with even margins all round, so the keyboard no longer squeezes it. Shrink it back to the orb to type.
Screenshot Shutter
When the app screenshots itself for a session, the screen flashes and the shutter clicks.
The flash comes after the capture, so it’s never in the picture.
Reduce Motion makes it a soft dim, and Dim Flashing Lights turns it off.
In a call the click plays through the call, so the agent doesn’t hear it.
In a voice call, say “look at this”
Calls Say What’s Still Running
When your request takes a while, the voice agent tells you what it’s working on instead of going quiet.
Calls Float in the Orb
Voice calls now float in the Living Orb for everyone, above every screen, while the message field stays yours.
Tap the orb to grow it into the call’s card, and drag up for the whole call and its transcript.
Drag the orb anywhere; it stays put as you switch sessions or open Settings.
Start a call from the session list too, with the call button beside Settings.
The Tray is gone: if you used it, calls float in the orb too.
Switch it off in Settings › Experimental › Calls › Living Orb.
Start a call, then open the session list: the orb comes with you
Quicker Send
A message you send now rises into its bubble along with the list, instead of waiting at the composer first.
Share Screen with Agents
Turn on Share Screen with Agents in Settings › Experimental › Calls, and during a call an agent can ask to see the app: tap Share to send it a picture, or Not Now.
Audio in Calls
Turn on Audio in Calls in Settings › Experimental › Calls, and during a call an agent can play music or a clip for you. It turns down while either of you speaks; pause or stop it above the composer.
Open Links from Calls
Turn on Open Links from Calls in Settings › Experimental › Calls, and during a call an agent can offer a link, like an Uber ride: tap Open to open it in its app, or Not Now.
Fold Questions Out of the Way
Drag a question down to fold it into a small bar above the composer, and tap it to bring it back. A failed answer now waits on Retry.
Steadier Following
A streaming reply stays pinned to the bottom without Working bouncing, and you can swipe the list from anywhere above the composer.
Model Names
The composer remembers model names while the model list loads or reconnects.
All Experiments
One switch at the top of Settings › Experimental turns every experiment on, including new ones as they arrive.
Switch one experiment off to skip it; it stays off next time too.
Turning All Experiments off puts back the switches you had before.
Experiments that ask for a permission stay a choice of their own.
Autocomplete, the plus menu’s photo sheet, the new server switch and project icons are now on for everyone.
One Picker and Living Orb are plain switches, and Call Tray is gone.
Open Settings › Experimental and switch on All Experiments
Find Older Sessions
Search in the sidebar now looks through every session, not just the recent ones, and scrolling to the bottom loads older sessions.
Switch Sessions by Voice
Asking your voice agent to open a session now closes the drawer and keeps your call connected.
Three Experiments Ship
The Living Orb, the New divider and image link previews are now on for everyone, with no switch.
Every call floats in the Living Orb; the old call bar is gone.
Coming back to a session, a New divider marks what arrived while you were away, when it doesn’t fit on screen.
Links straight to an image show the picture under the message.
Start a call from the composer and watch it float in the orb
Links and Audio on Calls
Open Links from Calls and Audio in Calls are now on for everyone, with no switch.
During a call an agent can offer a link, like an Uber ride: tap Open to open it in its app, or Not Now.
An agent can play music or a clip on the call. It turns down while either of you speaks; pause or stop it above the composer.
On a call, ask the agent to play some music
Editing Drafts
Editing a word in the middle of a draft keeps the cursor where you’re typing.
Scrolling After Loading
Returning to the app during a loading transition restores transcript scrolling immediately.
Wider Composer While Typing
With the keyboard up, the composer widens to a small, even margin, so long drafts wrap less.
Closing the Attachment Menu
Closing the attachment menu releases the session beneath it even during a layout change.
Steadier Launch
Opening the app no longer flashes “Reconnecting…” above the composer or nudges the session; the pill shows only when a reconnect takes a moment.
Scrolling Recovers Itself
If something invisible keeps a session from scrolling for more than a second, the app releases it.
Select Across a Reply
Hold or double-tap a word in a reply, then drag the handles across paragraphs, lists, code and tables.
Hold a handle just below the header or just above the composer and the reply scrolls, faster the closer you are to the edge.
Copy keeps list bullets and numbers, and table rows and columns. Quote adds the selection to the composer and keeps code fenced.
Hold a word near the start of a long reply, then drag the end handle down to the composer and hold it there
Scrolling Unsticks Itself
A session that sometimes wouldn’t scroll until you switched to another one now scrolls again on its own.
Steadier Server Connections
OpenCode tries all of a server’s addresses at once and uses whichever answers first, so it reconnects when you leave home without you switching your VPN off and on.
An address that worked on your home network is no longer tried first everywhere else.

A brief drop, unlocking your phone or pulling down Quick Settings no longer flashes a banner. Reconnecting appears after a few seconds, and Offline after about 12, or 4 when your phone has no network.
With a session open on a server paired with Tailscale, turn off Wi-Fi and keep working
Calls on Your Server’s Keys
Server Voice is now on for everyone, with no switch. Calls can use your OpenCode server’s keys, so this phone doesn’t need its own OpenAI key.
With Choose Automatically on, calls use the server you’re on, then your OpenAI key on this phone, then another saved server that’s ready.
If this phone and your server both have an OpenAI key, calls now use the server’s. To keep using yours, open Your OpenAI Account in Voice Provider and tap Use for Calls.
Gemini Live is now a provider too, on servers with a key for Gemini.
A call that can’t start says why and shows the button that fixes it.
Open Settings › Voice and tap Voice Provider
Clear a Title in One Tap
Rename Session and Rename Server now have a clear button, so you can start a new title without deleting the old one.
New Model Picker
Tap the model in the message box and the list grows out of it, with Favorites and Recent at the top and every provider below.
Tap the thinking level on a model’s row, like “high”, to change it without leaving the list.
Swipe or hold a row to add it to Favorites or take it out.
Search is at the bottom, and typing a level after a name, like “opus high”, picks both when you press Return.
Drag the grabber up for a taller list, or down to close it.
The new picker replaces the old Model sheet, and the One Picker switch is gone from Settings › Experimental.
Tap the model in the message box, then swipe a row to favorite it
Readable “Connecting via…”
While a call connects through a server, its “Connecting via…” line sits on glass, so it no longer runs into the messages behind it.
New Sessions Use Your Default Model
New sessions start on the model set as your default in OpenCode, at the thinking level you last picked for it, instead of the last session’s model.
Open a Reply Midstream
When you open a session while a reply is streaming, you can read what has already arrived as the reply continues.
Draw on Images
Point out a detail before asking about it.
Open an image full screen and tap the pen button. Choose a colour, draw, then tap Add to attach the marked-up image to your message. The original stays unchanged.
Circle the control you want moved in a screenshot, then describe where it should go.
Swipe Between Photos and Videos
Browse a session’s images and videos together.
Swipe to a video, then tap the pen button to mark up the current frame. Add attaches the marked-up frame without sending it.
Pause a demo on the screen that needs changing, circle the detail, and add it to your draft.
Named Servers From OpenCode Console
A server you pair from OpenCode Console arrives with its name, such as “Anomaly Box”.
Session Media
Browse a session’s images, videos, audio, files and public web links.
Choose Session Media from a session’s ⋮ menu. Media shows its images, videos and audio as tiles grouped by month or as a list, and Files and Links list its documents, pastes and web links.
Find the screenshot you sent this morning without scrolling back through the whole session.
Phone Icon for Calls in the Drawer
The call button beside Settings in the session list shows a phone, like the one in the message box.
Scripts in Background Work
Scripts the agent moves to the background show beside subagents and shells, and a subagent stays listed while its images, videos or scripts still run. Stop either from the list.
